newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DECLARES STATE BALKANBANK INSOLVENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DECLARES STATE BALKANBANK INSOLVENT.

text.p: The Sofia City Court has declared state-owned Balkanbank bankrupt on the basis of an insolvency claim filed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), a BNB official said on Monday.

"The court decided on Friday to declare Balkanbank insolvent and appointed Snezhana Basheva and Stoyan Stoyanov as administrators to handle the bankruptcy," an official from the BNB Legal Departement told Reuters.
The bank can appeal against the ruling within 14 days after it is published in the State Gazette whose next issue is due on Tuesday.
Balkanbank and court officials were not immediately available for comment.
The BNB put Balkanbank in receivership in September last year on the basis of a capital to risk assets ratio of minus 37.85 percent and outstanding payments of 5.47 billion levs.
It sought insolvency for Balkanbank through the courts at end-October.
Balkanbank owed 1.57 billion levs to the BNB, of which 592 million were collateralised debt, 1.63 million marks and $1.68 million, all collateralised, at end-1996.

Balkanbank is the ninth local commercial bank declared insolvent by courts so far out of a total of 17 state and private banks, or a third of Bulgaria's banks, against which the BNB has opened bankruptcy proceedings since May 1996.
It is also the third state Bulgarian bank ruled insolvent after Mineralbank and Economic Bank.

So far the BNB has withdrawn its insolvency claims against two of the 17 banks after they were bought - Mollovbank, which was re-named Eurobank, and Yambol Bank, renamed Bulgaria Invest Commercial Bank. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 911 88
